newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Bank in C$2.4 bln bid for London Ins.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank in C$2.4 bln bid for London Ins.

text.p: Royal Bank of Canada said on Friday it would offer C$27.50 a share to acquire all the outstanding common shares of London Insurance Group for a total of C$2.4 billion.
London Insurance's majority shareholder, Trilon Financial Corp said it had agreed to tender its 57-percent stake to the offer.
Royal Bank said it has lock-up agreements with both London Insurance and Trilon to support the offer.
The insurance company had revealed on Tuesday it was in talks with Canada's largest bank.
London Insurance's board of directors unanimously recommended that shareholders accept the offer.
The deal is slated to close in October.

Royal Bank said shareholders will have the option of accepting payment of C$27.50 cash, or a combination of C$16.50 in cash, 0.09 of a Royal Bank common share, and 0.22 of a new Royal Bank preferred share. The new preferred shares will have an issue price of C$25.00 per share and pay non-cumulative preferential quarterly dividends in the amount of C$0.325 per share to yield 5.20 percent.
The bank said Trilon has elected to accept payment in the above-described combination of cash, common shares and preferred shares.
The bid is conditional upon 90 percent of shares being tendered.

"Royal Bank's acquisition of London Insurance Group will enhance the competitiveness of two leading Canadian companies in the increasingly globalized and integrated marketplace for financial services," said Royal Bank Chairman and Chief Executive John Cleghorn.

London Insurance has more than C$5 billion in revenues and 11,000 employees and representatives. As at March 31, 1997 the group had C$25.1 billion in assets and C$33.3 billion in assets under administration.
"This deal will benefit our customers, our people and our shareholders," said London Insurance President and Chief Executive Fred Tomczyk.

"We will remain Canadian-owned and we will continue to operate as a vibrant going concern with our own management, our own headquarters in London, our own employees, and our own distribution network," he added.

Royal Bank said the lock-up agreements also prohibit London Insurance and Trilon from soliciting any further offers. If a higher value unsolicited competing bid is made by a third party, the bank has the right to increase its offer to match that offer. If the bank matches that offer, London Insurance and Trilon must continue to support the bank's offer.

If Royal Bank does not match that offer, and London Insurance modifies or withdraws its recommendation to shareholders to accept the Royal Bank offer, the support and lock-up agreements end and London Insurance must pay a fee of C$70 million to Royal Bank.
